misconceptions: Mistaking composed behavior for a failure to recognize risk.

words.sense: self-satisfied enough to overlook risks or needed improvements
misconceptions: Assuming outward calm means unjustified satisfaction with the status quo.

semantic_axes.description: Placid refers to calm behavior or conditions; complacent refers to self-satisfaction that blinds someone to possible trouble.

edges.boundary_rule: Placid refers to calm behavior or conditions; complacent refers to self-satisfaction that blinds someone to possible trouble.
clues_a: steady response in a stressful moment
clues_b: fails to prepare out of self-satisfaction

misconceptions.M1: Confuses placid with complacent by overlooking the defining difference: Placid refers to calm behavior or conditions; complacent refers to self-satisfaction that blinds someone to possible trouble.
misconceptions.M2: Assumes evidence for complacent necessarily proves placid; these are different tests.
misconceptions.M3: Overweights a later superficial detail instead of retaining or appropriately updating the original boundary evidence.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mara’s manner at the airport?

beats.text: Mara read quietly through a long flight delay while others raised their voices.
beats.reason: Her demeanor is peaceful, not careless.

beats.text: When the gate changed, she packed her bag and followed the new sign without fuss.
beats.decisive_clue: responded calmly while still paying attention to changes
beats.reason: She stays composed while responding appropriately to new information.

chains.feedback_short: Responded calmly while still paying attention to changes; she stays composed while responding appropriately to new information.
chains.feedback_deep: Placid means calm and undisturbed in manner; complacent means self-satisfied enough to overlook risks or needed improvements. She stays composed while responding appropriately to new information.
chains.contrast_rule: Placid refers to calm behavior or conditions; complacent refers to self-satisfaction that blinds someone to possible trouble.
